English Grammar: Determiners (Notes & Tricks)

Determiners kya hote hain?

Determiners aise words hote hain jo kisi Noun (Sangya) ke theek pehle aakar us Noun ko 'determine' (nishchit) karte hain. Yeh batate hain ki hum kitni cheezon ki baat kar rahe hain, ya kis specific cheez ki baat kar rahe hain.
(Asaan shabdon mein: Yeh Noun ke bodyguard hote hain, hamesha uske aage chalte hain).

Determiners ke Types:
1. Articles: A, An, The.
2. Demonstratives: This, That, These, Those.
3. Possessives: My, Your, His, Her, Their.
4. Quantifiers: Some, Any, Much, Many, Few, Little (Exams me yahi sabse zyada aate hain).

🔥 Golden Tricks (Quantifiers ke liye) - Part 1

1. Trick for 'Some' vs 'Any' (Kuch / Koi):

• Some: Iska use Positive (+) sentences mein hota hai. Agar kisi se Request (nivedan) ya Offer kar rahe hain aur ummeed 'Yes' ki hai, toh bhi 'Some' lagta hai.
• Any: Iska use Negative (-) sentences (jisme not, never, hardly ho) aur Questions (?) mein hota hai.

Examples:
• I have some good friends. (Positive)
• Would you like some tea? (Offer/Request)
• I do not have any money. (Negative)
• Do you have any extra pen? (Question)

🔥 Golden Tricks - Part 2

2. Trick for 'Much' vs 'Many' (Bahut):

• Much: Uncountable Nouns ke sath jise gina nahi ja sakta (jaise: water, milk, sugar, time, money). Yeh Matra (Quantity) batata hai.
• Many: Countable Nouns ke sath jise gina ja sakta hai (jaise: boys, books, chairs, rupees). Yeh Sankhya (Number) batata hai.

Examples:
• How much time do you need? (Time gin nahi sakte)
• How many students are present today? (Students gin sakte hain)

🔥 Golden Tricks - Part 3

3. The 'Little' Family Trick (Uncountable / Na ginne wali cheezon ke liye):

Yeh trick hamesha confuse karti hai, iska Hindi meaning yaad rakhein:
• Little (Negative): Na ke barabar. (Kaam nahi chalega).
• A little (Positive): Thoda sa. (Kaam chal jayega).
• The little (Specific): Jo thoda sa tha, woh pura ka pura.

Examples:
• There is little hope of his recovery. (Na ke barabar umeed hai)
• I have a little knowledge of computer. (Thoda gyan hai, kaam chal jayega)
• He drank the little milk left in the glass. (Jo thoda sa doodh bacha tha, woh sab pee gaya)

🔥 Golden Tricks - Part 4

4. The 'Few' Family Trick (Countable / Ginne wali cheezon ke liye):

Same 'Little' wali trick, bas ise un cheezon ke sath lagayein jinhe aap gin sakte hain.
• Few (Negative): Na ke barabar sankhya.
• A few (Positive): Kuch (Thodi sankhya).
• The few (Specific): Jo kuch the, woh sab.

Examples:
• He has few friends in this city. (Na ke barabar dost hain)
• A few students came to the class today. (Kuch hi bachhe aaye)

🔥 Golden Tricks - Part 5

5. Each vs Every (Pratyek / Har ek):

• Each: Jab group chhota ho aur hum group ke har ek member (individual) par focus karna chahein. (2 ya 2 se zyada ke liye).
• Every: Jab group bahut bada ho aur hum use ek samooh (general) ki tarah dekhein. (Hamesha 3 ya 3 se zyada ke liye).

Examples:
• Each student was given a certificate. (Class ke har ek bachhe ko focus kiya)
• India expects every man to do his duty. (Pure desh ke logon ki general baat hui)
